items.stem: Why must you check a project's licence before contributing or reusing its code?

options.text: Licences impose obligations (e.g. attribution or share-alike) that affect how code may be used and redistributed
options.rationale: Correct: licence terms are legally binding.

options.text: Licences only matter for paid software

options.rationale: They differ significantly, e.g. MIT vs GPL.

options.text: A licence prevents you from reading the code

items.explanation: Correct: licence terms are legally binding.

items.stem: What makes a good first open-source contribution?

options.text: A small, well-scoped change (e.g. a good-first-issue) that respects the project's process
options.rationale: Correct: small scoped changes are easier to land and learn from.

options.text: A sweeping rewrite of the core architecture
options.rationale: Too large and risky for a first PR.

options.text: A change opened without reading CONTRIBUTING.md
A PR with unrelated commits bundled together

items.explanation: Correct: small scoped changes are easier to land and learn from.

items.stem: Which practices improve the chance a pull request is merged? (Select TWO)

options.text: Write a clear PR description that links the issue it addresses
options.rationale: Correct: context helps reviewers evaluate the change.

options.text: Respond to review feedback constructively and update the PR
Bundle several unrelated changes into one PR
Skip running the project's tests locally
options.rationale: False; failing CI delays or blocks merging.
